sources.title: The Embedded Rust Book
extracted: Full chapter outline (no_std environment, tooling, memory-mapped registers, semihosting, panicking, exceptions, interrupts, peripherals)
Peripherals as State Machines: PAC read()/write()/modify() closures, Peripherals::take() singleton enforcement, constrain()/split()
Static Guarantees: typestate programming, into_af_push_pull-style compile-time transitions, zero-cost monomorphization
Portability: the micro-arch → PAC → HAL → board-crate layering, embedded-hal as the driver-portability seam
Concurrency: hardware non-reentrancy of exception handlers, `static mut` in handlers, multicore caveat, interrupt priority/nesting
sources.caveat: Cortex-M / STM32F3DISCOVERY examples throughout. The IDIOMS transfer to Espressif; the register names and `cortex-m` specifics do NOT.

sources.title: The Embassy Book
extracted: Executor model: cooperative polling, Poll::Pending yield, statically-allocated tasks via #[embassy_executor::task], no heap, fairness guarantee
embassy-time: Timer::at / Timer::after, default 32768 Hz tick (1000 Hz / 32768 Hz / 1 MHz selectable), per-platform Timer Driver required
embassy-sync: Mutex<RawMutexType, T>, Channel with Sender/Receiver, Signal, PubSubChannel
embassy-net: Ethernet/IP/TCP/UDP/ICMP/DHCP
InterruptExecutor for priority preemption across multiple executor instances
FAQ: cargo-call-stack for worst-case stack, cargo size for .data/.bss, opt-level="s" + lto="fat" + build-std=["core"] + panic_immediate_abort
sources.caveat: First-party HALs are stm32/nrf/rp/mspm0; ESP32 is listed as EXTERNALLY supported (via esp-rtos). Embassy-book HAL specifics do not apply to us — the executor/time/sync semantics do.

sources.title: esp-rs/esp-idf-hal (the std path)
extracted: Naming convention: repos prefixed `esp-idf-` are the std path; repos prefixed `esp-` are the no_std path
std path supports whatever ESP-IDF supports; no_std was written from scratch and is less complete but now covers most common peripherals
Practical tradeoff: the std path eventually requires reading ESP-IDF C; esp-hal is a plain cargo build, all Rust
sources.caveat: Read via search-result summary. Load-bearing for our clawft-edge-pad-idf crate, so re-fetch directly before any std-path migration decision.

sources.title: esp32-s3-rgb-touch-display agent — 2026-05-15 session learnings
extracted: The measured fix-B heap split: heap_allocator! in internal SRAM FIRST, then HEAP.add_region(psram_raw_parts) with MemoryCapability::External; only the framebuffer requests External
esp_alloc::psram_allocator! PANICS on ESP32-S3 N4R8 / AP_3v3 in linked_list_allocator hole.rs:331
esp-hal 1.0 has NO RGB-DPI bounce buffer (upstream issue #5262 open) — the reason the esp-idf port exists
#[esp_hal::ram] placement is required for a VSYNC ISR or you eat a 20-30 µs flash-fetch stall per fire
sources.caveat: Hardware-specific to the CrowPanel DIS08070H. The ALLOCATOR and ISR-placement lessons generalize; the panel timings do not.
